reviewer_summary.question: Why must a chosen word be processed before choosing the following word, and how do saved keys and values reduce repeated work?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Choosing blue uses is’s finished result; processing blue makes its own result while reusing unchanged earlier reading data separately at each layer.

findings.problem: A supplied practice input interrupts the actual word-input-to-reading path.

resolution.note: Remove the supplied-function detour. Keep the actual word inputs, prepared operands and match visible, then clip/add/name its amount inline. Hide future operation labels until the operation is taught.

findings.problem: The source-prepared number, product and practice input all equal 0.25, making jobs hard to distinguish.

resolution.note: Remove the extra practice input; explain that the source-prepared number depends only on The, while the match uses both reader and source preparation.

findings.problem: Another full layer of arithmetic crowds out the opening question before a word is chosen.

resolution.note: Retain the complete requested mechanism, with the stable concrete guide Finish is’s second layer → choose the next piece, and parallel known-operation rows instead of serial re-teaching.

findings.problem: The preparation comparison must retain the extra condition that prior finished results were also discarded.

resolution.note: Repeat text-only replay without earlier working results in both the count narration and displayed route label.
